**L2978 · A generated file with hand edits is a trap (third time in one session): markers, --check, outside-bytes proof, idempotency**

## A "generated" file with hand edits in it is a trap, and this is the third time in one session

MEASURED 2026-09-28 (ZABZ-TECH). Building the 0.1.7 preset migration, a converter emitted
`profiles/web/presets.generated.patch.yml`, and the installer wrote the same rows into a MANAGED BLOCK
inside the hand-maintained `profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`. Both worked. The danger is structural, not
a bug in either:

 * `scripts/make_zabz_preset.py` rewrites `presets/zabz/agent.cordis.yml` WHOLESALE, and the committed
 file had accumulated hand-authored owner rules (persona rules 8 and 9, the outbound-communication
 hard-stops, "ask him before a counterparty") that exist in NEITHER the generator NOR
 `presets/cordis-bg/`. Running it deleted 33 lines, and it was caught only because `git diff --stat`
 was read before committing. (LESSONS L2858.)
 * `scripts/make-preset-rows.mjs` emits a header comment naming the REMOVED package
 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets` in order to explain the rename -- and that comment was then read by
 the inventory scanner as a DEPENDENCY, producing an authoritative `BREAKS` against a candidate that
 breaks nothing.
 * The same class in the other direction: `profiles/mesh/cordis.patch.yml` keeps a comment naming the
 old package, handled correctly as `unverified` rather than `BREAKS`.

WHAT MAKES IT SAFE, and the rule to keep: a generated region must be (a) delimited by markers that are
checked to appear exactly once, (b) reproduced byte-for-byte by a `--check` that exits non-zero on
drift, (c) proven not to touch a single byte outside its markers, and (d) idempotent across repeats.
`make-preset-rows.mjs --install` now satisfies all four, and proves (c) by stripping the block from both
texts and comparing the remainders -- `86ede50abac9087e…` is the sha256 of the original file, so the
remainder is the original byte for byte.

AND THE SCANNER RULE NOW APPLIES EVERYWHERE: any consumer that extracts package names from config must
skip COMMENTS. A generated file's header is exactly where the removed names get documented, so a
comment-blind scanner turns good documentation into a false crisis. Fixed for YAML; fixed for scripts.

GENERALIZATION: never let a tool both generate a file and be the only thing that reads it, without a
marker-and-check contract. And always `git diff` before believing a generator.
